title: "Lesson 16: Clinical Notes (EHR) - Transformers / BERT"
---

## Introduction to the Domain

Clinical notes contain rich information not captured in structured fields. NLP can extract phenotypes, predict outcomes, and support coding. Transformers (BERT) dominate, but clinical variants (ClinicalBERT, BioBERT) and privacy constraints matter.

### Research background

Clinical notes contain rich information not captured in structured data. Alsentzer et al. (2019) released clinical BERT embeddings trained on MIMIC notes, and Devlin et al. (2019) introduced BERT. These works show how transfer learning can unlock clinical text, while raising privacy and fairness concerns.

**Citations:**
- Alsentzer E et al. Publicly available clinical BERT embeddings. *ClinicalNLP Workshop* (2019).
- Devlin J et al. BERT: Pre-training of deep bidirectional transformers for language understanding. *NAACL* (2019).

## Research Question

Can a transformer model classify or extract information from clinical notes, and what are the privacy implications?

## Open-Source Dataset

**MIMIC-III / MIMIC-IV (requires credentialed access) or i2b2 challenges.**

- Link: https://physionet.org/content/mimiciii/1.4/ (credentialed)
- Alternative (open): https://huggingface.co/datasets (search clinical notes)
- Size: large.
- Outcome: ICD codes, mortality, phenotypes.
- Notes: de-identified but re-identification risk; data use agreements.

## Practical Exercise

### Model to explore

Fine-tune a pretrained clinical BERT (e.g., `emilyalsentzer/Bio_ClinicalBERT`) with Hugging Face Transformers.

### AI prompts to learn this model

- "Explain transformers and self-attention to an undergraduate."
- "What is BERT, and why fine-tune a pretrained model for clinical text?"

### Starter code

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForSequenceClassification, Trainer, TrainingArguments
from datasets import load_dataset

model_name = "emilyalsentzer/Bio_ClinicalBERT"
tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForSequenceClassification.from_pretrained(model_name, num_labels=2)
print("loaded", model_name)
# ds = load_dataset("your_clinical_dataset")
# tokenize, train with Trainer(...)
```

### Suggested AI prompts

- "Why use a clinical BERT instead of general BERT?"
- "How do I handle long clinical notes (token limits)?"
- "What are the privacy risks of fine-tuning on clinical text?"

### Extensions

- Try zero-shot classification with a general LLM.
- Compare with TF-IDF + logistic regression baseline.
- Evaluate calibration and subgroup fairness.
